definitions.classParticipationAttendance: Individual. Frequent voluntary participation is expected; the professor cold-calls anyone who is silent. A quiz is given in the first 5 minutes of every class testing whether you looked at that day's readings and whether you are physically present, and those quiz scores count toward the participation grade. Worth 20% of the final grade.
definitions.mergerExercise: Individual. A merger exercise run near the start of the semester and overseen by TA John Kim. Data and instructions are provided; it requires light coding in R with step-by-step instructions, so no prior coding experience is needed. It is broken into a few separate assignments, but only the final assignment is turned in for a grade — the first 3 are practice/feedback only. Discussion in groups is encouraged but no one may complete another student's assignment. Worth 15%.
definitions.groupProjectAndPresentation: Group. In the second half of the semester you work in groups of 4 on a mock antitrust case. Students submit their top three case choices and the instructor team forms groups. Two students argue the government enforcement agency's position and two argue for the firm(s). Each team sends the professor a presentation plan 4-5 days in advance for comments. Each side gives a 10-minute presentation (plaintiffs first, then defendants), followed by class questions and a vote. The presentation plus the written slides constitute the final project; slides are uploaded to the course website on the day you present. Worth 20%.
definitions.assessments: Individual. Two closed-book exams. The midterm is a closed-book/internet exam given during the last class before fall break and is designed to check absorption of material to that point. The final is a closed-book exam covering all course topics, held during the official exam period. Together worth 45%.
definitions.readingsBracketConvention: Readings printed in [square brackets] in the schedule are included for background reference and are optional. Legal cases carry page numbers so you can focus on that specific part of the case. Readings labeled KW come from The Antitrust Revolution, Kwoka and White, 6th or 7th edition.
definitions.groupWorkIntegrity: No student's name should appear on a group project if the student has not substantively contributed to the production of the project. In group work all members are responsible for the integrity of what is submitted.
definitions.plagiarism: It is acceptable to refer to concepts, frameworks, and analytical tools from the readings or lectures without citation. It is unacceptable to quote or paraphrase analysis from another source and present it as your own.

gradingPolicy: Class Participation 20%; Merger Exercise 15%; Exam + midterm 45%; Class presentation and slides 20%. Laptop policy: no clamshell laptops open during class; a device lying flat on the desk is fine. Students with an excused absence should fill out the Excused Absence form on Canvas and contact Kimberly Jowers for access to the class recording.

officeHours.note: No regular office hours — email the professor for an in-person or Zoom appointment. See the TA first for logistical issues or small questions.
officeHours.details: Prof. Fiona Scott Morton, Evans Hall 3516. Administrative assistant: Kimberly Jowers — contact her for class recordings after an excused absence. TA: John Kim, who also oversees the merger exercise. Room: Evans Hall 2200. Email addresses and phone numbers are in the syllabus PDF and on Canvas.
